`minidb/executor.py` is implemented, but 13 of the 14 tests pass and `test_insert_reports_no_rows` fails. That test can't pass alongside another one, so this subtask will fail the validator as it stands.

`test_insert_reports_no_rows` expects an INSERT to return `row_count == 0`. `test_insert_without_columns_passes_values_through` expects `row_count == 1` for the same call, `execute_insert(InsertStmt("t", None, (7, "z", False)), store)`. Your spec and the `QueryResult` docstring both say INSERT returns 1, so I followed that. That choice is what makes the "reports no rows" test fail.

I can't edit the test file, so I haven't changed anything to make it pass. Making that test pass would break the other one and contradict the spec. The "reports no rows" test looks like it is wrong. Either it needs to be fixed or removed, or the spec has to change to say INSERT returns 0. Because one failing subtask holds the whole release train, someone needs to decide that before tonight.
